title: LAISS-assisted review reclassifies anomalous ZTF transients
summary: Expert review of 455 previously observed transients changed 16 normal labels to anomalous; the random-forest model flagged 11 of these. Spectra, light curves and host context supported the reclassifications. This is a retrospective study-level result rather than a count of newly observed events or newly established physical classes. Human review and similarity searches also contributed, so the entire retrospective sample is not attributed to the classifier.
ai_technology: LAISS random-forest anomaly classifier and similarity search
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Pacific Northwest National Laboratory

evidence.tested: Existing photometry and classification spectra were re-examined to support revised labels.
evidence.unknown: Anomaly categories depend on expert judgments; universal first-discovery priority and new physical mechanisms are not established.
evidence.ai_role: LAISS random-forest anomaly classifier and similarity search supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.
